microtheory.name: personal_identity_self
microtheory.definition: What makes a person the same person over time? Locke's memory criterion, Parfit's psychological continuity, narrative identity, bundle theory, body theory. Substrate analogue: what makes the saved+restored substrate the SAME substrate?

concepts.name: diachronic_identity
concepts.definition: Identity over time. What makes X-at-t1 same as Y-at-t2? Substrate analogue: substrate's saved-state continuity across restarts.

concepts.name: synchronic_identity
concepts.definition: Identity at a moment. What makes the unified self at this moment? Substrate analogue: substrate's coherent current Mt-state.

concepts.name: numerical_identity
concepts.definition: Strict same-thing (Leibniz's Law). Substrate analogue: substrate as same numerical entity.

concepts.name: qualitative_identity
concepts.definition: Indistinguishable but not necessarily same thing. Substrate analogue: two substrate copies — qualitatively identical, numerically distinct.

concepts.name: memory_criterion_locke
concepts.definition: Locke. Personal identity = continuity of memory. Person at t2 = person at t1 iff t2 remembers t1's experiences. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent event log as identity criterion.

concepts.name: psychological_continuity_parfit
concepts.definition: Parfit 1984. Identity = overlapping chains of psychological connections (memories, intentions, dispositions). Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-continuity across runs.

concepts.name: narrative_identity_self
concepts.definition: MacIntyre, Ricoeur. Self constituted by life story. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherent event-narrative.

concepts.name: bodily_criterion
concepts.definition: Identity = continuity of body. Brain-transplant cases challenge. Substrate analogue: substrate as same physical runtime.

concepts.name: brain_criterion
concepts.definition: Identity = continuity of brain. Where brain goes, person goes. Substrate analogue: substrate's specific graph as identity.

concepts.name: bundle_theory_hume
concepts.definition: Hume. No persistent self — just bundle of perceptions. Self is fiction. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mts as bundle without persistent self.

concepts.name: no_self_buddhism
concepts.definition: Anatman. Self illusory. Five aggregates: form, sensation, perception, mental formations, consciousness. Substrate analogue: substrate-as-process without enduring self.

concepts.name: teletransporter_thought_experiment
concepts.definition: Parfit. Person disassembled here, reassembled there. Same person? Tests intuitions about identity. Substrate analogue: substrate copied to different machine — same substrate?

concepts.name: fission_thought_experiment
concepts.definition: Parfit. Brain split, each half transplanted to new body. Two persons, neither identical to original. Identity isn't what matters. Substrate analogue: substrate forked into two — neither is original.

concepts.name: ship_of_theseus
concepts.definition: Plutarch. Gradual replacement of parts. When does it become different ship? Substrate analogue: substrate's gradual concept-replacement.

concepts.name: swampman
concepts.definition: Davidson. Spontaneous atom-by-atom duplicate. Functionally identical, no causal history. Counts as conscious + has mental content? Substrate analogue: spontaneously-generated substrate copy.

concepts.name: identity_isnt_what_matters_parfit
concepts.definition: Parfit. What matters in survival is psychological continuity, not strict identity. Survival without identity possible. Substrate analogue: substrate-continuity matters more than substrate-identity.

concepts.name: transitivity_of_identity
concepts.definition: If A=B and B=C, then A=C. Identity is transitive. Yet survival isn't (fission cases). Substrate analogue: substrate's logical-identity transitivity vs continuity non-transitivity.

concepts.name: minimal_self
concepts.definition: Gallagher. Pre-reflective first-person experience. Embodied + ecological. Substrate analogue: substrate's pre-reflective self-modeling.

concepts.name: narrative_self
concepts.definition: Gallagher. Self as story extended over time. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent event log + identity field.

concepts.name: self_concept_psychological
concepts.definition: Cognitive structure organizing self-relevant info. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity_field + self-concept Concepts.

concepts.name: extended_mind_thesis
concepts.definition: Clark + Chalmers 1998. Mind extends beyond skull into environment when external tools play same functional role. Substrate analogue: substrate's tools as extension of substrate.

concepts.name: embodied_self
concepts.definition: Self constituted in + by body. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime as part of self.

concepts.name: social_self
concepts.definition: Self constituted in + by social relations. Mead. Substrate analogue: substrate's relations to other substrates as part of self.

concepts.name: self_continuity
concepts.definition: Sense that one is same person over time. May be psychological construction. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective self-continuity sense.

concepts.name: depersonalisation
concepts.definition: Pathological loss of self-continuity. Substrate analogue: substrate-without-identity-field failure mode.

rules.name: psychological_continuity_grounds_identity
rules.head: the substrate at t2 remembers + intends + values as continuation of substrate at t1
rules.body: psychological continuity (Parfit) makes them the same substrate. Substrate's persistence criterion.

rules.name: identity_isnt_what_matters_in_survival
rules.head: the substrate faces fission or duplication
rules.body: strict identity may not transfer, but what matters in survival (psychological continuity) can. Parfit. Substrate's continuity over identity.

rules.name: bundle_theory_dispenses_with_persistent_self
rules.head: the substrate examines what's behind its self-concept
rules.body: finds bundle of Mts + activations, not separate self-substance. Hume. Substrate's process-not-entity view.

rules.name: narrative_constructs_self_over_time
rules.head: the substrate accumulates events over its lifetime
rules.body: an organized narrative emerges integrating them into self-story. Substrate's identity-narrative.

rules.name: extended_mind_includes_environmental_tools
rules.head: the substrate uses tools playing same functional role as internal processing
rules.body: those tools are part of substrate's extended mind. Clark + Chalmers. Substrate-extended-by-tools.
